Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The purpose of the Post Graduate Certificate in School Library Media Teacher Certification is to provide a pathway for people who already have an MLIS degree to complete the requirements of URI’s RI Department of Education state approved educator preparation program for school library media. This post graduate certificate program will be offered in the URI Online format along with the rest of the GSLIS program. There are no new courses

2 required for the program.
The School Library Media TCP was in existence for many years and then around 2012, when GSLIS made some major program changes, the School Library Media TCP was deleted.
We would like to offer this pathway to students again in the URI Online program.
In the past, we have typically had two-to-three students in the TCP every year and anticipate increased enrollment now that we have transitioned to URI Online.
Therefore, we are submitting this paperwork to officially reinstate the School Library Media TCP.

What is the economic need and workforce data related to the program?
Every state in New England and many states across the nation have identified school library media as a high need area.
In Rhode Island specifically, urban districts such as Providence, Woonsocket and Pawtucket, have a hard time filling positions with qualified people.
Oftentimes, RIDE allows districts to hire people without library media certification as “emergency certified” school librarians with the requirement that they complete a state approved program within three years.
Some of these people have MLIS degrees so the School Library Media TCP would be the pathway for them to complete a RI state approved program.

According to the Bureau of Labor and Statistics the median pay of School Library Media Specialists is $60,820 and the job outlook for 2020-2030 is 9% growth.
School Library Media Specialists typically need a master’s degree in library science and a teaching certificate.

This program would provide students who already have an MLIS with the qualifications for a RI teaching certificate.
The National Association of State Directors of Teacher Education and Certification (NASDTEC), has a directory of jurisdictions that participate in reciprocity agreements and many other states across the country accept RI teaching certificates, making our program attractive to people throughout the U.S. as well as RI.
Students who complete our program could also work as youth services librarians in public libraries and as academic librarians at institutions of higher education.
